title: Chest X-ray: signs, effusion, pneumothorax, TB, lung tumours, sarcoid
subject: Radiology
anchor: Name the sign first: each CXR sign maps to one diagnosis (silhouette, air bronchogram, Golden S, Westermark, Hampton hump, Pancoast).
Silhouette sign localises the lesion: right heart border = right middle lobe, left heart border = lingula, right hemidiaphragm = right lower lobe, aortic knob = left upper lobe.
Primary TB = Ghon focus + hilar nodes (Ghon complex); post-primary (reactivation) TB = apical/posterior upper lobe with cavitation.

tables.title: CXR sign → diagnosis
head: Sign
Diagnosis
rows: Alveolar (airspace) consolidation: pneumonia, pulmonary oedema, ARDS
Right upper lobe collapse due to a central mass
Focal oligaemia distal to a pulmonary embolus
Peripheral wedge-shaped pleural-based opacity of pulmonary infarct
Enlarged central pulmonary artery in PE
Apical mass: Horner syndrome, C8–T1 pain, rib destruction
Bronchiectasis (bronchus wider than its accompanying artery)
Sarcoidosis; Garland (1-2-3) sign = right paratracheal + bilateral hilar nodes
Lung abscess, post-primary TB, cavitating squamous carcinoma
Concentric / laminated calcification of a nodule

points: Pleural effusion: blunting of the costophrenic angle needs roughly 200 ml on PA erect film; lateral decubitus shows smaller volumes; ultrasound is the most sensitive bedside test and guides aspiration.
Tension pneumothorax is a clinical diagnosis: immediate needle decompression, not an X-ray.
Miliary TB: innumerable 1–3 mm nodules uniformly distributed; HRCT is more sensitive than CXR.
Foreign body aspiration in a child: obstructive emphysema (air trapping) on the affected side, best on expiratory or lateral decubitus film; mediastinum shifts toward the normal side on expiration.
Lung cancer: central masses are usually squamous or small-cell; peripheral masses usually adenocarcinoma; cavitation favours squamous.
A solitary nodule is benign if stable ≥2 years or with central, laminated, diffuse or popcorn calcification.

traps.stem: Opacity with air bronchogram and no volume loss
traps.fix: Air bronchograms mean patent airways: consolidation. Collapse shows volume loss with shift toward the lesion.
Treat immediately with needle decompression; do not wait for imaging.

cards.text: Westermark sign = {{c1::focal oligaemia}} distal to {{c2::pulmonary embolism}}; Hampton hump = {{c3::pleural-based wedge infarct}}.

cards.front: Silhouette sign: loss of the right heart border means disease in?
cards.back: Right middle lobe (left heart border = lingula).

cards.front: CXR contents of the Ghon complex?
cards.back: Primary parenchymal focus (Ghon focus) plus ipsilateral hilar lymphadenopathy.

cards.text: Signet-ring sign suggests {{c1::bronchiectasis}}; best test is {{c2::HRCT}}.

cards.front: Foreign body in the bronchus: CXR finding in a child?
cards.back: Unilateral obstructive emphysema (air trapping), best on expiratory or lateral decubitus film.

verify: Standard radiology texts (Felson, Radiopaedia); volume thresholds approximate

title: Cardiac silhouettes on CXR: CHD shapes, rib notching, MS, pericardial effusion, constriction
subject: Radiology
anchor: Silhouette first: boot, egg-on-string, snowman, scimitar, water-bottle, 3-sign, double density each point to one lesion.
Plethora (shunt vascularity): ASD, VSD, PDA, TGA, TAPVC. Oligaemia: TOF, pulmonary stenosis, Ebstein, tricuspid atresia.

tables.title: Cardiac shape → lesion
head: Shape / sign
Lesion
rows: Tetralogy of Fallot (upturned apex, concave pulmonary bay, oligaemic lungs)
Transposition of great arteries (narrow pedicle, plethora)
Partial anomalous pulmonary venous return to the IVC (scimitar syndrome, hypoplastic right lung)
Coarctation of the aorta (intercostal collaterals); appears after ~5–6 years
Straight left heart border, double density, splayed carina, Kerley B lines
Pulmonary venous congestion / left heart failure

points: Pericardial effusion needs a few hundred ml to enlarge the silhouette; echocardiography is the investigation of choice and detects small effusions.
Coarctation: bilateral inferior rib notching; reverse-3 (E) sign on barium swallow marks the oesophageal indentation at the coarctation.
Constrictive pericarditis: calcification best on lateral film or CT; echo/CMR show septal bounce and thickened pericardium.
Kerley B lines (short horizontal septal lines at the lower lateral periphery) mean interstitial oedema.

traps.stem: Boot-shaped heart with decreased pulmonary vascularity
traps.fix: TGA is egg-on-string with plethora; boot with oligaemia is TOF.

traps.stem: Rib notching in a 2-year-old with coarctation
traps.fix: Notching appears after ~5–6 years; absence in a child does not exclude coarctation.

cards.back: Supracardiac total anomalous pulmonary venous connection.

cards.text: Boot-shaped heart = {{c1::Tetralogy of Fallot}}; egg on string = {{c2::transposition}}.

cards.back: Curvilinear vein draining right lung into IVC (PAPVC, hypoplastic right lung).

cards.text: Rib notching affects ribs {{c1::3–9}} and spares {{c2::1–2}}.

verify: Standard radiology texts; sparing of ribs 1–2 per classic teaching

title: Acute abdomen imaging: pneumoperitoneum, obstruction, volvulus, barium signs, gallbladder/biliary
subject: Radiology
anchor: Erect chest X-ray for free air; CT abdomen is the most sensitive and the next step in a stable patient.
Small bowel dilated >3 cm with valvulae conniventes crossing the lumen; large bowel >6 cm (caecum >9 cm) with haustra that do not cross.
Ultrasound first for gallbladder; HIDA for acute cholecystitis (non-filling gallbladder); MRCP for ducts; ERCP is therapeutic.

tables.title: Abdominal / GI sign → diagnosis
head: Sign
Diagnosis
rows: Rigler (double wall) sign, football sign, cupola sign, falciform ligament sign
Sigmoid volvulus (bird's beak on contrast enema)
String sign of Kantor, cobblestone, skip lesions
Calcified wall; associated with carcinoma risk
Portal venous gas vs biliary gas
Portal: peripheral (bowel ischaemia). Biliary: central (gallstone ileus, post-ERCP)

points: Toxic megacolon: colon >6 cm with systemic toxicity; avoid barium enema and colonoscopy.
Acute cholecystitis on USG: stones, wall thickening >3 mm, pericholecystic fluid, sonographic Murphy sign.
CBD above ~6 mm with an intact gallbladder is dilated (wider after cholecystectomy and with age).
Pneumatosis intestinalis with portal venous gas in a sick adult is bowel infarction until proved otherwise.

traps.stem: Pneumoperitoneum in a stable patient: best next test
traps.fix: CT abdomen is the most sensitive and shows the source; unstable patients go to theatre.

traps.stem: Investigation for CBD stones that also treats them
traps.fix: MRCP is diagnostic only; ERCP is diagnostic and therapeutic.

cards.back: Small bowel obstruction + pneumobilia + ectopic gallstone: gallstone ileus.

cards.text: Double bubble sign = {{c1::duodenal atresia}}; corkscrew = {{c2::midgut volvulus}}.

cards.front: Non-visualisation of gallbladder on HIDA means?

verify: Standard radiology texts; dimensions are conventional cut-offs

title: Bone imaging: tumour signs, Pott spine, paediatric hip, rickets/scurvy, Honda sign
subject: Radiology
anchor: Match the lesion to its sign: sunburst/Codman = osteosarcoma; onion peel = Ewing; soap bubble = giant cell tumour; popcorn = chondroid; punched-out = myeloma.
Pott spine: paradiscal vertebral destruction with disc preserved until late, paravertebral abscess; pyogenic spondylitis hits the disc early.
DDH: ultrasound (Graf) in infants under about 4–6 months; X-ray after the femoral head ossific nucleus appears.

tables.title: Bone lesion → imaging sign
head: Lesion
Sign
rows: Sunburst, Codman triangle; metaphysis of long bones, 10–20 yr
Soap-bubble, eccentric lytic epiphyseal lesion after physeal closure
Blown-out expansile cyst with fluid-fluid levels on MRI
Nidus <1.5 cm with sclerosis; night pain relieved by NSAIDs
Cotton-wool skull, picture-frame vertebra, ivory vertebra
Cupping, fraying, splaying of metaphysis; widened growth plate
Wimberger ring, Pelkan spur, Trümmerfeld zone, Frankel line
Flattened, fragmented femoral epiphysis; Waldenström stages
Klein line fails to cross the epiphysis; ice-cream slipping off the cone

points: Hilgenreiner line is horizontal through the triradiate cartilages and Perkin line is vertical from the lateral acetabular edge; the femoral head ossific nucleus normally lies in the inferomedial quadrant.
MRI is the investigation of choice for local staging of bone sarcoma; CT chest looks for lung metastases.
Skeletal TB: bone scan can be negative; sclerosis is late.
Osteoid osteoma is best seen on thin-slice CT and treated by radiofrequency ablation.

traps.stem: Eccentric lytic epiphyseal lesion in an adult
traps.fix: An eccentric soap-bubble epiphyseal lesion after physeal closure is a giant cell tumour.

traps.stem: Disc space narrowing with endplate erosion early in spinal infection
traps.fix: TB preserves the disc early; early disc loss suggests pyogenic infection.

cards.text: Onion-peel periosteal reaction = {{c1::Ewing sarcoma}}; sunburst + Codman = {{c2::osteosarcoma}}.

cards.back: H-shaped uptake on bone scan in sacral insufficiency fracture.
Line along the superior femoral neck fails to intersect the epiphysis.

title: Neuro imaging: head trauma, SAH, tumours, classic MRI signs, Circle of Willis
subject: Radiology
anchor: Non-contrast CT head first for trauma, suspected haemorrhage and acute stroke; MRI DWI is the most sensitive for early infarct.
Epidural: biconvex, does not cross sutures. Subdural: crescent, crosses sutures, not dural reflections (falx, tentorium).
Suspected SAH: NCCT within 6 h is very sensitive; if negative and still suspected, lumbar puncture for xanthochromia; CT angiography locates the aneurysm.

tables.title: Neuro imaging sign → diagnosis
head: Sign
Diagnosis
rows: Butterfly glioma crossing corpus callosum, ring enhancing
Cyst with mural nodule in cerebellum
Hyperdense midline vermis mass in a child

points: Acute blood is hyperdense on CT; subacute subdural can be isodense; chronic is hypodense.
ECA branches (8): superior thyroid, ascending pharyngeal, lingual, facial, occipital, posterior auricular, maxillary, superficial temporal.
Circle of Willis: anterior communicating joins the ACAs; posterior communicating joins ICA to PCA; berry aneurysms are commonest at the anterior communicating/ACA junction.
Diffuse axonal injury: small haemorrhages at grey-white junction, corpus callosum and dorsolateral brainstem; MRI (SWI/GRE) shows best.

traps.fix: Epidural does not cross sutures; a crescent crossing sutures is subdural.

traps.stem: Thunderclap headache with normal CT at 10 hours
traps.fix: After 6 hours do LP for xanthochromia or CTA.

cards.text: Hot cross bun sign: {{c1::MSA-C}}; hummingbird sign: {{c2::PSP}}.

cards.front: Cystic cerebellar lesion with mural nodule?

cards.text: ECA has {{c1::8}} branches; the terminal branches are {{c2::maxillary and superficial temporal}}.

verify: Standard neuroradiology texts; SAH CT within 6 h per ACEP/AHA guidance

title: Nuclear medicine, PET and radiotherapy: isotopes, scans, fractionation, brachytherapy
subject: Radiology
anchor: Tc-99m: 140 keV gamma, half-life 6 h, from a Mo-99 generator; the most used isotope.
PET: F-18 FDG (half-life ~110 min); positron annihilation gives two 511 keV photons at 180°.
Radiotherapy: dose in gray; conventional 1.8–2 Gy/day, 5 days a week; the 4 Rs are repair, repopulation, reassortment, reoxygenation.

tables.title: Scan / isotope → use
head: Scan / isotope
Use
rows: Dynamic renal: GFR / tubular secretion, obstruction
Thyroid cancer ablation (beta); I-123 for imaging
Pulmonary embolism when CTPA is contraindicated

tables.title: Radiotherapy modalities
head: Modality
Key point
rows: Photons and electrons; standard external beam
Bragg peak: dose at depth, sparing tissue beyond
Co-60 sources (192–201 by model), intracranial stereotactic radiosurgery

points: PET false negatives: low-grade tumours, mucinous tumours, bronchioloalveolar carcinoma; normal high uptake in brain, heart, bladder.
Hyperfractionation spares late-responding tissue; hypofractionation uses larger doses per fraction.
Hypoxic cells are radioresistant; oxygen enhancement ratio ~3 for X-rays.
Gamma Knife source count depends on the model.

traps.fix: I-131 is therapeutic (beta); I-123 is for imaging.
DMSA is for cortical scarring; DTPA/MAG3 are dynamic.

cards.text: Tc-99m half-life {{c1::6 hours}}; energy {{c2::140 keV}}; generated from {{c3::Mo-99}}.

cards.back: Maximum dose at depth with no exit dose: protons/carbon ions.

cards.text: 4 Rs of radiobiology: {{c1::repair, repopulation, reassortment, reoxygenation}}.

title: X-ray, ultrasound, Doppler, contrast and FAST basics
subject: Radiology
anchor: kVp sets penetration and contrast; mAs sets film blackening (quantity); ~99% of tube energy becomes heat (tungsten target).
Higher ultrasound frequency = better resolution, less penetration: curvilinear 2–5 MHz for abdomen, linear 7–15 MHz for small parts and vessels.
FAST: free fluid in the hepatorenal (Morison) pouch is the commonest early positive site.

tables.title: Probe / test
head: Probe / test
Use
rows: Vascularity around ectopic pregnancy / corpus luteum
Cumulative dose; lithium fluoride thermoluminescent dosimeter

points: Ultrasound cannot image through bone or gas; MRI avoids ionising radiation.
FAST views: pericardial, hepatorenal, splenorenal, pelvic; e-FAST adds lung views for pneumothorax (absent lung sliding).
Gadolinium: nephrogenic systemic fibrosis risk in severe renal failure, mainly with older linear agents.
Distance and shielding reduce dose (inverse square law); grid reduces scatter.
